questions.q: The editorial sets two sentences side by side: “God is great, so I am not great” and “God is great, so you are not great.” What difference does it see?
options: The two mean exactly the same
Not quite. The article says: The first breeds humility and self-improvement; the second breeds pride and conflict.
The second is the more accurate
Not quite. The article says: The first breeds humility and self-improvement; the second breeds pride and conflict.
The first is for scholars, the second for everyone
Not quite. The article says: The first breeds humility and self-improvement; the second breeds pride and conflict.
The first breeds humility and self-improvement; the second breeds pride and conflict
Yes. The command is addressed first to oneself.
questions.rationale: “‘God is great, therefore I am not great,’ this will engender a feeling of responsibility within you… ‘God is great, therefore, you are not great’; this will beget a psychology of pride.”

questions.q: The heir to a great motor company said, “I am not a car. I’m a spiritual soul.” What does the article conclude from such cases?
options: Fame brings more peace than money
Not quite. The article says: Wealth serves the body but cannot fill the soul’s emptiness; that is answered only by turning to God.
Wealth serves the body but cannot fill the soul’s emptiness; that is answered only by turning to God
Well read. Amid plenty, one can still feel a void.
The wealthy should give up business
Not quite. The article says: Wealth serves the body but cannot fill the soul’s emptiness; that is answered only by turning to God.
Success depends on one’s family name
Not quite. The article says: Wealth serves the body but cannot fill the soul’s emptiness; that is answered only by turning to God.
questions.rationale: “No amount of wealth and fortune can supply the needs of the human soul… The only true answer to this quest for a sense of spiritual fulfillment can be found in turning to God.”

questions.q: A man asked the Prophet what to do in a certain matter, and was told, “Consult your heart about it.” What does the article understand by this?
options: Each person may make his own religion
Not quite. The article says: Islam accords with human nature – sound common sense points the same way.
Islam accords with human nature – sound common sense points the same way
Right. A religion of nature.
Feelings matter more than knowledge
Not quite. The article says: Islam accords with human nature – sound common sense points the same way.
Advice from others is never needed
Not quite. The article says: Islam accords with human nature – sound common sense points the same way.
questions.rationale: “By the heart, the Prophet meant common sense. That is, what one’s common sense tells would likewise be the demand of Islam.”

questions.q: In the parable, doves complained to a Sufi after his disciple killed one of them. What exactly was their complaint?
options: The disciple had not asked permission
Not quite. The article says: The travellers came dressed as men of God, so the birds felt safe – yet they behaved as hunters.
The travellers had camped too near the trees
Not quite. The article says: The travellers came dressed as men of God, so the birds felt safe – yet they behaved as hunters.
The travellers came dressed as men of God, so the birds felt safe – yet they behaved as hunters
Yes. A spiritual person is one from whom no harm comes.
Birds should never be eaten
Not quite. The article says: The travellers came dressed as men of God, so the birds felt safe – yet they behaved as hunters.
questions.rationale: “All of you came here in the garb of Sufis yet acted as hunters… When we saw you in the guise of Sufis, we thought that we were safe with you.”

questions.q: According to the Hadith quoted, what is the highest form of worship?
options: To pray for the longest time
Not quite. The article says: To pray as if you were seeing God.
To pray in a beautiful building
Not quite. The article says: To pray as if you were seeing God.
To pray in the largest gathering
Not quite. The article says: To pray as if you were seeing God.
To pray as if you were seeing God
Correct. A felt closeness to Him.
questions.rationale: “The Prophet Muhammad said the highest form of worship is to pray as if you were seeing God.”

questions.q: Of those who work in a joint effort, which kind does the article say actually “make history”?
options: Those who lead from the front
Not quite. The article says: Those for whom the work itself is the reward, who do not mind receiving less credit than their due.
Those who insist on full payment first
Not quite. The article says: Those for whom the work itself is the reward, who do not mind receiving less credit than their due.
Those for whom the work itself is the reward, who do not mind receiving less credit than their due
Well reasoned. They remember duties, not rights.
Those who receive the most praise
Not quite. The article says: Those for whom the work itself is the reward, who do not mind receiving less credit than their due.
questions.rationale: “Those alone can perform great tasks and attain to greatness, for whom the accomplishment of the task itself is the real reward.”

questions.q: “Whatever misfortune befalls you is of your own doing” (42:30). Why does the article find hope in this?
options: Because nothing can be changed
Not quite. The article says: If our problems lie in our own hands, so do their remedies – we need not wait on others.
Because misfortune is always deserved
Not quite. The article says: If our problems lie in our own hands, so do their remedies – we need not wait on others.
If our problems lie in our own hands, so do their remedies – we need not wait on others
Yes. One can re-plan and try again.
Because others will soon suffer too
Not quite. The article says: If our problems lie in our own hands, so do their remedies – we need not wait on others.
questions.rationale: “It offers great hope for us; in that it has placed our problems in our own hands. It has not left us to be dependent on the charity and compassion of others.”

questions.q: By what comparison does the article explain the role of angels?
options: A school with many teachers
Not quite. The article says: A large factory whose machines need attendants – the universe has unseen ones.
A market with many traders
Not quite. The article says: A large factory whose machines need attendants – the universe has unseen ones.
A large factory whose machines need attendants – the universe has unseen ones
Right. In the factory the hands are visible; here they are not.
An army with many soldiers
Not quite. The article says: A large factory whose machines need attendants – the universe has unseen ones.
questions.rationale: “Countless angels are appointed to ensure the proper functioning of the great factory of the universe.”

questions.q: In what basic respect do angels differ from human beings, according to the article?
options: Angels have no free will and always obey; man can choose between right and wrong
Exactly. Hence man alone is tested.
Angels live only in the heavens
Not quite. The article says: Angels have no free will and always obey; man can choose between right and wrong.
Angels cannot communicate
Not quite. The article says: Angels have no free will and always obey; man can choose between right and wrong.
Angels are fewer in number
Not quite. The article says: Angels have no free will and always obey; man can choose between right and wrong.
questions.rationale: “They have no free will. They always obey God and never displease Him. Man, on the other hand, has been given free will and can choose between right and wrong.”

questions.q: Saad ibn Abi Waqqas directed a battle from a rooftop and was thought a coward, until it was known he was crippled by illness. What lesson does the article draw?
options: Commanders should always fight in front
Not quite. The article says: Do not believe something discreditable about a person without finding out the full facts.
Do not believe something discreditable about a person without finding out the full facts
Well read. The whole picture often differs.
Soldiers may disobey a weak leader
Not quite. The article says: Do not believe something discreditable about a person without finding out the full facts.
Illness should be kept secret
Not quite. The article says: Do not believe something discreditable about a person without finding out the full facts.
questions.rationale: “Whenever something malevolent is said about other, it should not necessarily be believed without further investigation.”
